details: Tensions remain high as Iran outlines six conditions for reopening the Strait of Hormuz, including US force withdrawal, an end to proxy warfare, financial reparations, sanctions relief, and lifting the naval blockade. US President Trump indicated a focus on economic pressure, noting Iran's "huge inflation" and economic distress. Oil prices are rising due to prolonged disruption concerns, with Brent crude nearing $85 per barrel. Additionally, the US Treasury recently sanctioned digital asset exchanges for funding Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) and facilitating illicit finance.
title: Iran Sets Demands for Strait of Hormuz Reopening Amid US Economic Pressure

details: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has publicly rejected a 15-point US-backed peace plan for the Gaza Strip, affirming that Israeli forces will not withdraw until Hamas is "genuinely disarmed." This move marks a notable divergence from President Trump's peace efforts. Meanwhile, Iranian-backed Houthi rebels in Yemen have attacked the port city of Mocha and a Saudi Aramco refinery in Jizan, raising concerns about the conflict expanding to other strategic shipping routes in the Red Sea and further disrupting oil supplies.
title: Netanyahu Rejects US-Backed Gaza Peace Plan, Vows Continued Presence

details: Ukraine continues to target Russian energy infrastructure, with multiple refinery strikes in early August and attacks on Russia's shadow fleet tankers in the Black Sea and Sea of Azov. These actions contribute to the tightening of distillate markets globally, with diesel futures experiencing significant gains. Total refinery capacity offline due to ongoing conflicts, including those in Russia and Saudi Arabia, is nearing 5 million barrels per day, approximately 6% of global operating rates.
title: Ukraine Intensifies Attacks on Russian Energy Infrastructure

details: The US Senate failed to gather enough votes to advance the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act before its August recess, postponing any decision until at least mid-September 2026. This bill aims to clarify regulatory oversight for various crypto assets. Despite the regulatory delay, US spot Bitcoin Exchange-Traded Funds (ETFs) recorded their strongest week of inflows since April, attracting $853.54 million in the week ending August 7, with BlackRock's IBIT receiving a substantial portion. Bitcoin's price held near $65,200, supported by a softer-than-expected US jobs report and a weaker US dollar, which also eased concerns about further Federal Reserve rate hikes.
title: US Crypto Clarity Act Stalls, Bitcoin ETFs See Strong Inflows
